subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should transient plugin state use an agent-scoped extension of the existing plugin-state API, remain in shared plugin state with explicit agent namespacing, or stay private until concrete external-plugin requirements are documented?
rationale: This selects a permanent public Plugin SDK and database-ownership boundary; source inspection establishes overlapping facilities but cannot determine the intended external contract.

options.title: Extend Existing State API
options.body: Add explicit agent scope to the existing plugin-state abstraction, reusing its namespace, expiry, cleanup, and migration behavior rather than creating a parallel facade.

options.title: Document Shared Namespacing
options.body: Keep the current shared plugin-state store and document a canonical agent-ID namespace convention when strict database-level agent separation is unnecessary.

options.title: Require Concrete Cases First
options.body: Defer SDK expansion until affected external plugins provide state shapes, lifecycle needs, size limits, and restart reproductions.

recommendation.title: Extend Existing State API
recommendation.body: Add explicit agent scope to the existing plugin-state abstraction, reusing its namespace, expiry, cleanup, and migration behavior rather than creating a parallel facade.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily a public plugin API and ownership-boundary decision, matching their recent plugin API review history.
